confirmations: run() holds `body` (at most limit+1 bytes, already size-checked) before the returncode check at line 244, so a whole-output equality test there adds no new read and no new limit
ToolFailure today keeps args/str as 'bwrap_tool_failed' and only a bounded returncode; adding one strict-bool attribute keeps the existing str() checks working for probe() and runtime_version()

diagnostic_probe catches ToolFailure separately from the generic RuntimeError branch, so restricting the mapping to stage=='unshare' and type(code) is int and code==1 and attr is True fits cleanly; the bwrap stages stay nonzero_exit
No consumer reads the stage reason: the workflow only runs diagnostic-probe and the workflow test doesn't check reasons, so adding a reason value breaks nothing downstream

Both lines match util-linux's err(EXIT_FAILURE, _("unshare failed")) format of '<prog>: unshare failed: <strerror>\n' when argv0 is /usr/bin/unshare. EPERM and EACCES map to the two strerror strings, and the error comes before exec, so no other output is expected
Not inferring host policy (AppArmor, capabilities, sysctl) is honest; translated or unknown output correctly stays nonzero_exit
